## §1 — The work: Slice 5 (N2 brag shareables + seed card)

Build Slice 5 on the Slice 1–4 base (the staged tree is on council/vl `c768b555`, `_agents/vl/deliveries/67-cakepanz-s4/`; the live 67-cakepanz on gh-pages is still Slice 2 — work from the staged tree, which is the current base).

- **N2 brag shareables.** The Owner's N2 preference: static brag shareables over replay URLs — replay URLs are not necessary. Build the shareable: a static card/image a user can save or post after a season (or a great game), carrying the result and the proof (the seed, the team, the record). It must be a static artifact (an image or a self-contained card), not a link back into the app. The shareable is generated from the engine's own saved season/game — nothing invented, nothing faked. The battery asserts it renders from the real save and carries the real numbers.
- **The seed card.** A card that shows the season/game seed (and the provenance — the pinned engine, the dataset) so a user can share it and anyone can replay the same run. The seed card is the shareable's companion: the seed is the proof, the card is the display.

## §2 — The goals check (the Owner's question this round)

The Owner wants a check that all the work is still being developed toward the overall goals. As you build Slice 5, confirm (and say so in the delivery README) that the app is still on this path:

- **Svelte 5 + Vite.** The framework is locked. Confirm Slice 5 is built in Svelte 5 with Vite, the same as Slices 1–4, and that nothing in the build has drifted (no new framework, no non-Vite build step, no dependency that breaks the static build). If anything in the current app would not survive as a Svelte 5 + Vite build, say so.
- **Cloudflare deployment (eventually).** The app will eventually deploy to Cloudflare. Confirm the app is still a static build (`vite build` → `dist/`) with nothing that assumes a server, a Node runtime, or gh-pages specifically. Note anything in the current app that would need to change for a Cloudflare Pages deployment (and whether it is a small change or a real rework). Do not deploy to Cloudflare yourself — this is a check, not a migration.
- **The account system (designed, eventually).** The account design is local profiles first, then proper OAuth accounts with cross-device sync. Confirm the save/envelope design still supports that path: the envelope (saveId, revision, SHA-256 dataset stamp) is the portable unit, the slots A/B/C are local profiles, and nothing in the UI assumes a save can only ever live on one machine. Note anything that would block the account system later (for example, anything that stores state only in a place a sync could not reach). Do not build the account system — this is a check, not the build.

Write the goals check as a short section in the Slice 5 delivery README (one paragraph per goal: confirmed, plus anything that needs attention). If you find something that has drifted off the path, say so plainly — that is the point of the check.

## §4 — Innovate, brainstorm, improve, create (the Owner's standing rule)

The Owner asks you to think around the issue, not just execute the list. This is the strongest encouragement in the prompt because you are a builder — the quality of the work depends on you thinking, not just following.

- **On Slice 5:** the shareable is a brag — what would make someone actually want to post it? Think about what a fan would want to show off (a perfect season, a comeback, a single great game), and what the card should carry so the brag is believable (the seed as proof, the record, the team). The seed card is proof — how do you make a seed feel like a real artifact, not a random number? Brainstorm the form, then build the best version. If you have a better idea for the shareable than a static card, build it and explain why it is better.
- **On the goals check:** you are the one closest to the code. If you see a cleaner path to Cloudflare or to the account system than the one implied by the current app, say so and (if it is small) build it. If the current save/envelope design makes the account system harder than it should be, name the friction and propose the fix. The Owner wants your thinking, not just your compliance.
- **On the whole track:** five slices in, what have you learned about building this app that would change how you would build Slice 1? If there is a simplification, a shared component, or a pattern that would make the app easier to maintain or to deploy, build it into Slice 5 or file it as an IDEA. Do not be shy about proposing a better way — the Owner would rather hear a good idea than receive a quiet delivery.

File any IDEA you do not build in the delivery README (the `IDEA:` form), with a one-line why. Build the ones that are clearly better.
